sample_unit: emergency room diagnostic images (US, CT, X-ray)

links.outcome: GPT-4V accuracy identifying modality, anatomical region, and pathology on ER images versus senior radiologists
links.effect: Modality 100% (221/221), anatomical region 87.1% (189/217), pathology 35.2% (76/216); pathology accuracy 9.1% in US, 36.4% in CT, 66.7% in X-ray.
links.quote: GPT-4V identified the imaging modality correctly in 100% of cases (221/221), the anatomical region in 87.1% (189/217), and the pathology in 35.2% (76/216).

links.outcome: Reliability of GPT-4V as standalone diagnostic tool; diagnostic hallucination rate
links.effect: Pathology identification only 35.2% correct; authors report diagnostic hallucination rate >40% and state it cannot be trusted as a standalone clinical tool.
links.quote: Although GPT-4V shows promise in radiological image interpretation, its high diagnostic hallucination rate (> 40%) indicates it cannot be trusted for clinical use as a standalone tool.

screen.reason: The study evaluates the diagnostic performance and hallucination rate of GPT-4V on a dataset of retrospective emergency room radiological images without testing any deployment safeguard or organizational practice.
